title: There is, there isn’t — asking about the neighborhood
title_target: এখানে কি বাজার আছে? — è-kha-né ki ba-jar a-chhé?
goal: Say that something is or isn’t somewhere — and discover that Bengali prepositions stick to the end of the noun as endings instead of standing in front of it.
bekal: ask এখানে কি … আছে? and answer it
attach the place ending -এ · -তে · -য় to place names
use এখানে, ওখানে, সেখানে, কাছে, and দূরে
build sentences in the order place — thing — আছে

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — On the veranda, asking about the neighborhood
dialogs.intro: First morning. Ani wants to know what’s around the guesthouse. Watch the words ending in -এ and -তে: they aren’t new words, just words you already know plus an ending that means “in” or “at”.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Rahim Bhai, is there a market here?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Yes, it’s very close. At the end of the street.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: And a pharmacy? Is it far?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: No, not far. There’s one next to the market.
lines.literal: no, far-at — not. market-of — side-at — one — is.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Is there an ATM in this lane?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Not in this lane, but there are two on the main road.
lines.literal: this — lane-in — isn’t, but — big — road-on — two — are.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: A tea stall? I need tea in the morning.
lines.literal: tea-of — shop? morning-in — my — tea — needed.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Ha ha! There’s one right in front of the house. It opens at six in the morning.
lines.literal: ha ha! right — house-of — front-at — is. morning — six-o’clock — from — open.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Wonderful! And the internet? Is there Wi-Fi in the room?
lines.literal: wonderful! and — internet? room-in — wifi — is?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: There is, but it’s not very fast. It works well on the roof.
lines.literal: is, but — very — fast — not. roof-on — well — runs.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Me, Mitali, and Mother. Father isn’t here — he’s in Chittagong.
lines.literal: I, mitali, and — mother. father — isn’t, he(polite) — chittagong-in.

notes: **Bengali prepositions stick on as endings — your first structural surprise.** English says **in** the house; Bengali says বাড়ি**তে**, “house-in”. The ending has three shapes, chosen by the last letter of the word: ⓐ ends in a consonant → **-এ** (ঘর → ঘরে, বাজার → বাজারে, টেবিল → টেবিলে); ⓑ ends in a vowel → **-তে** (বাড়ি → বাড়িতে, গলি → গলিতে); ⓒ ends in আ → **-য়** (ঢাকা → ঢাকায়, রাস্তা → রাস্তায়). ⚠️ These aren’t three different rules but one ending adjusting itself to be easy to say — just as English “a” becomes “an” before a vowel.

**আছে has one form for all things.** One book or a thousand books, it’s still আছে. No *is* versus *are*, no masculine or feminine. It changes only when the **subject** is I or you (আছি, আছ, আছেন) — and you learned that in Unit 1.

⚠️ **The negative of “there is” is a separate word: নেই.** Never say *আছে না*. The only correct form is **নেই** *néi*, and it **doesn’t change for anyone**: আমি নেই, তুমি নেই, বইটা নেই, তারা নেই — one form for the whole world. This is some of the best news in Bengali grammar, so learn it right now.

**“There is something somewhere” runs in a different order from English.** We say “there is a market here”; Bengali says **এখানে বাজার আছে** — “here — market — is”. Place first, thing second, verb last. ⚠️ This order holds for almost every Bengali sentence you’ll make, so get used to it now: **the verb always goes at the end**.

**To ask “is there …?” just slip in কি.** এখানে বাজার আছে (there’s a market here) → এখানে **কি** বাজার আছে? (is there a market here?). Nothing is flipped, nothing moves — no “is there” inversion as in English, just one small word added, usually after the first word. The voice rises at the end too.

**কাছে (near) and দূরে (far) already have the -এ ending built in.** কাছ means “nearness”; কাছে means “at nearness”, i.e. “near”. That’s why you’ll often see **বাজারের কাছে** — “market-of nearness-at”, i.e. “near the market”. The **-এর · -র** ending there is the possessive marker, and Unit 4 covers it fully.

⚠️ **আম্মা · আব্বা or মা · বাবা?** In Muslim families in Bangladesh, father and mother are usually called **আব্বা** *abba* and **আম্মা** *amma*; in Hindu families in West Bengal, **বাবা** *baba* and **মা** *ma*. All of them are understood everywhere. Just remember one thing: বাবা means **father**, not baby.

grammars.title: The place ending: -এ · -তে · -য়
after: **The same ending also means “in/on/at” for time**: সকালে (in the morning), রাতে (at night), সোমবারে (on Monday), জানুয়ারিতে (in January). One ending for both place and time — just as English uses “in” for “in the house” and “in the morning”.
⚠️ **For people, the ending isn’t -এ but -র কাছে.** Don’t say *রহিমে*; the correct form is **রহিমের কাছে** (“near Rahim”, i.e. “with Rahim”). Bengali doesn’t put people inside a place.

grammars.title: আছে and নেই
after: ⚠️ Look at the last row: **আছি** changes with the subject, but **নেই stays নেই**. Bengali drops all those changes as soon as the sentence becomes negative — very economical, and one more thing you don’t need to memorize.

blocks.title: Three sentences for surviving on the street
items: **এখানে কাছে কি … আছে?** (*è-kha-né ka-chhé ki … a-chhé*) — “Is there a … near here?” Fill in the blank with anything: ব্যাংক, টয়লেট, ওষুধের দোকান.
**… কোথায়?** (*… ko-thay*) — “Where is …?” The shortest, most useful sentence in any language. বাথরুম কোথায়? স্টেশন কোথায়?
⚠️ **এখানে নেই।** means “it’s not here” — an answer you’ll hear often. Don’t be thrown when নেই stands alone with nothing else; it’s a complete sentence, like answering just “none”.

blocks.text: One habit worth knowing from the start: if you ask someone on the street for directions, the answer is often **much longer than you can follow** — plus some arm-waving. That’s not condescension; Bengalis feel it’s shameful for a host to leave a stranger confused. Just accept it with **ধন্যবাদ**, walk in the direction shown, then ask the next person. Asking twice is no shame at all.

vocab.en: there is, is (for things and third persons)

exercises.prompt: Add the right place ending: -এ, -তে, or -য়.
Put the words in the right order. Remember: place — thing — আছে.

items: There’s a bank near the market.
The tea stall is in front of the house.

answers: ঘরে — বাড়িতে — ঢাকায় — টেবিলে — রাস্তায় — গলিতে
এখানে বাজার নেই। — ঘরে চেয়ার নেই। — আমি ঢাকায় নেই। — টেবিলে কিছু নেই।
এখানে বাজার আছে। — এই গলিতে এটিএম নেই। — বাড়ির সামনে চায়ের দোকান আছে। — বাড়িতে কে আছে? — বড় রাস্তায় দুটো ব্যাংক আছে।
এখানে কি ওষুধের দোকান আছে? — না, এখানে নেই। — বাজারের কাছে ব্যাংক আছে। — ঘরে কেউ নেই। — আমি ঢাকায় আছি। — চায়ের দোকানটা বাড়ির সামনে।
